title: Judges choose judges in India
sources: S. P. Gupta v. Union of India (1981)
SC Advocates-on-Record Assn. v. Union of India (1993, 2015)

quiz.q: The NJAC was struck down in:
quiz.why: Right. In October 2015, in the Fourth Judges case.

lines.say: In most countries, the government appoints judges.
In India, senior judges choose them. How did that happen?

data.headline: The collegium: three cases and one Act

beats.say: In most countries, the government appoints judges. In India, senior judges choose them. How did that happen?

lines.say: In 1981, the First Judges case gave the government the upper hand.
The Second, in 1993, created the collegium. The Third, in 1998, set it at the Chief Justice and four senior-most judges.

beats.say: In 1981, the First Judges case gave the government the upper hand. The Second, in 1993, created the collegium. The Third, in 1998, set it at the Chief Justice and four senior-most judges.

lines.say: In 2014, Parliament replaced it with a National Judicial Appointments Commission.
In 2015, the Supreme Court struck that down, citing judicial independence.
